headline: High-risk default interaction: Goose can write/egress and Pipecat can relay shared-bus content to third-party AI services, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and run shell commands; Pipecat runs on a shared bus and can move text through voice/chat pipelines. That creates a plausible bridge where Goose-authored files or messages become Pipecat inputs. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so injected instructions could be parsed as content.
conditions: IF Goose writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file or MCP channel that Pipecat consumes
IF Pipecat forwards shared-bus text into an LLM or agent prompt without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable shared filesystem handoff between the agents
Require provenance labels on all Goose outputs before Pipecat ingests them
Insert a manual review step for any text passed from Goose to Pipecat
Restrict Pipecat to trusted, schema-validated inputs only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement at the bus boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, and its network egress is broad; Pipecat handles text, audio, video, and conversation state and can call many third-party model services. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive code or conversation data can flow from Goose into Pipecat and then out to external APIs. The profiles do not show isolation or redaction by default.
conditions: IF Goose and Pipecat share files, messages, or conversation state
IF Pipecat is configured to send shared text/audio to any listed external STT/LLM/TTS provider
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Turn off Pipecat integrations that forward content to third-party APIs
Redact secrets from Goose outputs before any handoff
Limit Goose to non-sensitive directories only
requires-engineering: add per-field data-loss prevention at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and git-state modification; Pipecat supports shared-bus concurrency and multiple instances. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or repo, concurrent writes and git changes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. No locking or coordination primitive is documented in either profile, so the unsafe default is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF either agent performs edits while the other is concurrently reading or committing the same files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Add a manual merge review before commits
requires-engineering: implement file locks or a coordinator for shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code, shell commands, and MCP actions; Pipecat can route text through LLM and transport services. If Pipecat treats Goose output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious Goose response can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing speech without verification. The profiles show no built-in verification step between them.
conditions: IF Pipecat consumes Goose output as a prompt, transcript, or task plan without validation
IF Pipecat triggers downstream API calls or spoken responses based on Goose-produced facts
mitigations: Require human approval before Pipecat acts on Goose output
Add a verification step that checks Goose claims against source data
Constrain Goose to produce structured outputs only
Log and diff Goose outputs before downstream use
requires-engineering: add policy gates for action-taking based on upstream agent output

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles source code and local files, while Pipecat handles audio, video, images, text, and analytics/metrics and can send data to many external providers. That combination can create retention, residency, or consent mismatches if regulated content enters the shared flow. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so the safer severity is medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data, recordings, or secrets are routed from Goose into Pipecat
IF Pipecat forwards that data to a provider whose residency or retention terms differ from the operator's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared pipeline
Disable analytics/metrics for sensitive sessions
Review provider residency and retention settings before enabling integrations
Add a short data-classification checklist before handoff
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement
